UPGRADE THE LOCAL AI SUPPORT, deskUnsloth. Design, 2026-10-09. Facts checked at 8924c0dc. Rulings live verbatim in the item they decide.

VISION (Andy's words): the local agent (qwen, on its own node, port 11111) becomes a real party at the desk: it knows what is talked about, its node is "it's sandbox and it's toolset", secured against it, and Andy configures memory, models and agent personas with their tools from a browser. "disregart the ollama agent, i want it to read along for now." And, out of the first item's scope but in the vision by his word: "that agent node should be a puppet of mine, where i can configure it's deskUnsloth remotely, sort of like we do with appFaceApp" and "the permission set may change with every deskUnsloth configuration". And where it goes (his, 2026-10-09): "picture this: a whole goal, designed for one agent persona, with its model configuration paired with it's tool-access-configuration, will tackle the same goal, while i sleep, event descending the dependency tree of that process...." Agents with standing orders, tied to one standing item with its own verification, come after this goal. His purpose for this goal (2026-10-09): "My goal would be, it can help me sketch a design while i wait for the day i get more tokens for claude." So the first achievement is the context item's first slice: one document, the box, discussed at length.

THE ITEMS, IN ANDY'S ORDER
0. API introspection retrofit: every verb declared on both doors (goal/G10.5): the core work, split off 2026-10-09 ("a big enough task for one item, it will require grants for core files"); blocks 1.
1. Endpoint introspection in OpenAI tool shape: the tool list for a key, stripped to its grants at ask time; the agent reads it (his named dependency).
2. The local agent node secured against its agent: puppet-dom, design-complete, then closed by him on 2026-10-09 as out of scope for now (the first slice speaks only to the desk); its box keeps the design for the tools slice.
3. Context auto-built from the desk goal for the local agent: title, box, last lines and AGENTS go with each line; addressed lines only; one config.
4. Configuration manager: VRAM, models and agent personas: out of scope by his word of 2026-10-09 ("oos"), closed by him the same day; the first configuration is two hand-edited files, the context item's; the screen is a later goal's.
6. streamClerver: set aside as its own goal, goal/G11, by his word of 2026-10-09; the item here was deleted by him the same day.

TOOLING DEFERRED, his (2026-10-09): "tooling is deferred for this goal. deskUnsloth simply will route between agent and desk". The introspection half waits for the tools goal; whether the retrofit still goes first here is his call.
SCOPE SETTLED, his (2026-10-09): "the toolset depends on the api retrofit, and i figured: enough for 1 goal." This goal is the retrofit (goal/G10.5) and the context item (goal/G10.3); the introspection half (goal/G10.1) waits for the tools goal and awaits his Close.

Four items design-complete on 2026-10-09: 0, 1, 2, 3; the design of the goal is complete, the gap check done; BUILD ORDER, his (2026-10-09): "retrofit, then context." Next his End design and Go on the retrofit, where his core-file grant waits; wsl-claude writes each red, cw builds, wsl verifies. Every item: a suite red on today's code first; the builder never writes its own tests.

No red Q stands on the goal (2026-10-09): a persona is a configuration with a tool set, not a key and not a node; the Grants app is not involved for the local agent.

THE ORDER, DECIDED by Andy on 2026-10-09, answering which of the two to Go first: "retrofit, then context." So the first Go is API introspection retrofit: every verb declared on both doors (goal/G10.5), where his core-file grant waits, and Context auto-built from the desk goal for the local agent (goal/G10.3) follows it. Endpoint introspection in OpenAI tool shape (goal/G10.1) sits between them by the chain, feeding the tools slice that the two closed items hold.

[loop.js] To secure the Local Agents Node against its own agents while maintaining a human interface, you should implement **strict role-based access control (RBAC)** and **isolated execution environments**.

Key measures include:
*   **Human-in-the-Loop Gates:** Require explicit human authentication and approval for any agent-initiated actions that modify node state or access sensitive data.
*   **Principle of Least Privilege:** Grant agents only the minimum permissions necessary for their specific tasks, preventing them from escalating privileges or accessing unrelated resources.
*   **Sandboxing/Containerization:** Run agents in isolated containers or sandboxes to contain any potential malicious behavior and prevent lateral movement within the node.

WHAT: deskUnsloth, on the local agent node, builds the standard tool entries from its own node's AGENTS family, which the retrofit provides: AGENTS.introspect lists the verbs that have a file ({items: [{key, label}], more}), AGENTS.<verb> answers that verb's file (its description and, for a loopback verb, its shape by hand), and the generic api answer gives a process server's shapes. DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-09)
1. His own node is protected by the peerPost authentication that exists; what this item protects is the agent's node against the agent itself. The agent node is his puppet (relay-state/owner.json naming him); the owner door takes his signed commands and runs them over the whole node surface, as a loopback client would (the group filter went with cleanup/G1.7).
2. The restriction per persona is its configured tool set, handed to the model by deskUnsloth alone (goal/G10.1, goal/G10.4): a persona is a configuration on the one agent node, not a key and not a node each; the Grants app is not involved for the local agent. 3. Puppet-dom, the same for every puppet and nothing per puppet, three refusals by name on a puppet node: peer.post to a key outside its contacts; the grant verbs (jobs.authGrant, authRevoke, authRelabel), a puppet authorizing nobody to anything, reads of the grants staying; a contact write (contact.accept, block, unblock, label, forget, setSenders) from its own loopback door, contacts being the owner's to write through the owner door. 4. A feature of one puppet lives in its appServer: the face's routing to face-owners (who are contacts the owner wrote) and deskUnsloth; the face puppet's features may later move into an appServer, an aside for another goal.

CONTEXT AUTO-BUILT FROM THE DESK GOAL FOR THE LOCAL AGENT. Design-complete 2026-10-09; facts at 512e59d3; Andy's words are in this chat.

WHAT: each call deskUnsloth makes to the model is built fresh from the desk, nothing kept between calls. In the window: the system prompt (the desk's AGENTS text and the persona's preamble), the goal's box and the item's box asked of the desk through deskClient, the persona's tools (second slice), and the item's chat as a rolling window of its newest lines, the oldest dropped. The window, in his words: MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH minus the goal and item boxes, and the two subtractions the call needs, the system prompt and the answer room (answerTokens), the tool list joining in the second slice; sizes in tokens by bytesPerToken from the configuration.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-09)
1. KISS: deskUnsloth speaks to the desk through the same deskClient server the agents use, in a loop, deskUnsloth the mediator, as today.
2. The context is the current goal's as the desk says it; a coder agent following the current goal as the claudes do. Standing-order agents are a later goal.
3. Boxes, not the file: currentGoal.json is the whole goal, 161 KB with every chat, beyond the window and stale on the agent node.
4. Two files for starters in deskUnsloth's state folder, out of git: the configuration (persona, preamble, model, context limit) and the connection (loop.json's key and url). No UI yet; the configuration manager is out of scope.
5. The first persona is Levant: preamble "you are 'Levant' (a genius i knew when i was a lead engineer at ATI technologies, later absorbed by AMD)", model unsloth/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B-GGUF (tool use, 12 GB; the DeepSeek R1 8B, a reasoning model without tool use, a possible second persona later), contextLimit 8192 to start, answerTokens 1024, bytesPerToken 4. The file is in this chat.
6. This goal is the first slice alone: one document and a remembered conversation, no tools, deskUnsloth routing between agent and desk and nothing more (his, 2026-10-09: "tooling is deferred for this goal. deskUnsloth simply will route between agent and desk"). The second slice, the persona's tools and the scoped file tools, is the tools goal's.
7. The agent answers lines addressed to it (its nick) and JOBs only, starts at the present, never the backlog, keeps the posting rules (3 lines, a question only when meant, its own name, no [loop.js]).
8. The cap bites on packets only: the context never leaves the agent's box; the chat is read in pages (item.chat, chat.search) and a long answer goes back as several lines under the room, split at paragraphs; a file travels as the fileServer's chunks. The streamClerver is Fake-streaming in SpiritOS: The StreamClerver (goal/G12).
9. OUT OF SCOPE OF goal/G10 (Andy, 2026-10-09, under the context item: "oos"). The first configuration is two hand-edited files, built by the context item (goal/G10.3); this screen is for a later goal. The item waits for his Close or Delete. What follows is the shape as argued, for that later goal.

WHAT: a shell app in three panels. Resource tuner: the serving process as a server job, its memory and unsloth settings (quantization, context window, attention) as manifest args, so start and restart are the node's; a VRAM reading is new, and the estimate says it is one. Model registry: the serving process's own model list, searchable. Persona creator: name, role, system prompt, sampling; its tools are the node's include list and grant rows chosen with the Grants app's path selector; no access levels (the door is loopback-only), no tokens (identity is a key).

WHY (Andy, 2026-10-09): "i want a configuration manager, that allows me to configure my dedicated VRAM and unsloth to use that memory optimally, list available models, and create agent-personas with those configurations. these agent configurations also will carry with them an authorization scheme for the loopback interface, so the "tools" that and agent gets are dependent on configuration." The three-panel sketch (the local agent's text) he called "an awesome start".

TODAY (8924c0dc): no such app. The Grants app gives, sees and revokes grant rows; a node runs only the servers its include list names (config.setModules); a node-operated server starts with its manifest args and a state folder of its own.

ANDY (2026-10-09): "1. the permission set may change with every deskUnsloth configuration", "2. that agent node should be a puppet of mine, where i can configure it's deskUnsloth remotely, sort of like we do with appFaceApp". So the configuration manager runs on Andy's node and configures the agent node as a puppet over the relay, the way the VPS face node is run; the persona's grant rows live on the agent node and change with each configuration.

OUT OF SCOPE OF goal/G10, a goal of its own later. Andy (2026-10-09, here): "nah, we make the streamClerver a separate goal, oos.

deskUnsloth, will only learn to speak to the desk, through the same deskClient server that you do, exept its in a loop and it's deskUnsloth that is the mediator. KISS." Its block on the context item is lifted; it waits for his Close or Delete. What stands below is the shape for that later goal.

WHAT: a faked stream between two nodes over peerPost, Andy's shape (2026-10-09, under the context item): a set of peerPost verbs that agree on a hash of both parties' public keys, reversed for the other side, and a stream-connect; the relay routes the packets as it does today; each packet one page under MAX_PAYLOAD, in order, both directions. The clerver is a process server (as chatClerver is), not the node's bones.

WHY (Andy, 2026-10-09): "well, on the model side, a MAX_PAYLOAD is NEVER going to hold ... maybe this whole thing depends on a two-sided-fileServer based Fake-stream?", "or we just implement a "streamClerver", that fakes streaming.....", "... but the fileServer we'd have to bastardize, and a streamClerver would be simple ...", "and the router would "stream" just as it is today.", "it is quite a different approach to the fileServer.", then "let's take out the "streamClerver" and make that an item this all depends on."

TODAY (512e59d3): no stream exists; a file travels as the fileServer's 6000-byte chunks ({command: chunk, start, length}, fileTransfer); a conversation as the chat's bounded pages (item.chat, chat.search); the context between deskUnsloth and the model goes over local HTTP, uncapped.

RULED, Andy (2026-10-09, here): "i think just the chat. this item however, is about the shape of a streamClerver and it's WAY simpler than i thought.

it basically fakes a telnet connection, except it's completely bidirectional and endless, and survives server outages and all." So the first cargo is the chat, and the shape is a faked telnet line: each side keeps its place per direction (a cursor, as deskClient keeps its place at the desk); every packet carries its number; a side that comes back asks from its cursor and the other resends from there, so an outage loses nothing; nothing is ever closed; the key hash names the line; a packet is one page.

TO SETTLE (red Qs): whether it blocks the context item alone (as added) or every item of the goal; the verbs are new node-side traffic between two clervers, so peer review and Andy's yes on the verb names.

TESTS FIRST: a suite red on today's code with two scratch nodes: the connect by the key hash, pages in order both ways, each under the room, a refused third party; the builder never writes its own tests.
